historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Phenylalkylamine calcium-channel blockers

starting.description: Papaverine's known smooth-muscle-relaxing and antispasmodic effects, including its use for intestinal colic, supplied a working natural-product lead for the synthetic D365/verapamil line, as reported retrospectively by Davies and Hollman.

inspiration.description: The molecular-development starting point was papaverine, an opium alkaloid with known smooth-muscle-relaxing and intestinal antispasmodic effects. Subsequently, observed cardiac effects of already synthesized verapamil and prenylamine led to recognition of calcium antagonism; that later mechanistic clue did not precede synthesis of the drugs.

steps.description: Papaverine's observed smooth-muscle relaxation and intestinal antispasmodic use preceded and, according to Davies and Hollman, led to the D365 analogue line.
Dengel's invention specified a synthetic phenylacetonitrile series for coronary vasodilatation and reported D365's experimental activity relative to papaverine.
The later history reports that the D365 compound was developed as verapamil, entered angina trials in 1961, and was marketed as Isoptin.

Fleckenstein investigated unexpected cardiac depression with the already synthesized coronary drugs verapamil and prenylamine. Their similarity to calcium withdrawal and reversibility with calcium helped establish the calcium-antagonist concept, named in 1969.

design.description: Researchers synthesized a novel phenylacetonitrile series and studied its coronary-dilating activity; the historical accounts call D365 a synthetic analogue of papaverine, a benzylisoquinoline. This is an appreciable architectural change, but the sources read do not specify the complete sequence by which it was achieved.

circumstances.description: The patent-stage search for coronary vasodilatation was planned; Fleckenstein described the later recognition of calcium antagonism while investigating unexpected cardiac depression as a chance discovery.

evidence.locator: Full article, single historical paragraph, sentences on papaverine's smooth-muscle and intestinal effects and Knoll's D365 analogue.
Description, objectives and D365 pharmacology following Examples 6–19; patent text on coronary blood flow and comparisons with papaverine.
Section 'Prenylamine paved the way to developing modern calcium antagonists', Fleckenstein quotation and following paragraph.
Page 198, right-hand column, paragraphs on papaverine and Dengel's analogue programme.

limits: The papaverine-to-verapamil classification concerns the assigned verapamil line, not separate dihydropyridine or benzothiazepine families.

Prenylamine contributed a distinct co-observation to the calcium-antagonist concept, but the sources read do not establish that it followed the papaverine-to-verapamil chemical-development pathway; the judgment is not an origin classification of prenylamine's separate molecular line.
conflicts: Davies and Hollman 2002 (E1) date the D365 analogue to 1957; Hollman 1991 (E5) says May 1959. The sources share an author and the discrepancy remains unresolved.
gaps: The original Dengel/Knoll notebook or project rationale has not been read; the specific papaverine-to-D365 causal attribution rests on retrospective accounts rather than the patent's pharmacological comparator alone.
Fleckenstein's 1983 original review was read only as an abstract, with an additional passage reproduced by a later review; the contemporaneous 1964 experimental report has not been read.
The 1962 Haas-Haertfelder original pharmacology article was located as metadata without an abstract and was not read.
The intermediate chemical-development sequence and the precise date of first D365 synthesis are not resolved by the materials read.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: Papaverine's clinical use for intestinal colic and its smooth-muscle effects supplied a precedent for Knoll's D365 or verapamil line.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: A retrospective causal account; the later cardiovascular indication should not be represented as an original bedside discovery.
